```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```


```{r}
getwd()
scale_data_1 <- read.csv("/home/zzeng1/Innovation80/Innovation80/Scale Data - Sheet1.csv")

# Check the first few rows of the dataset to ensure it's loaded correctly
head(scale_data_1)

```
```{r}
# Check the class of the variables to ensure they are numeric
class(scale_data_1$Attendance)
class(scale_data_1$Meaning.Level)

# If they are not numeric, convert them to numeric
scale_data_1$Attendance <- as.numeric(scale_data_1$Attendance)
scale_data_1$Meaning.Level <- as.numeric(scale_data_1$Meaning.Level)

```



```{r}
colnames(scale_data_1)
# Convert blank values in Attendance and Meaning.Level to NA
scale_data_1$Attendance[scale_data_1$Attendance == ""] <- NA
scale_data_1$Meaning.Level[scale_data_1$Meaning.Level == ""] <- NA

# Remove rows with NA values in Attendance or Meaning.Level
cleaned_data <- scale_data_1[!is.na(scale_data_1$Attendance) & !is.na(scale_data_1$Meaning.Level), ]

# Create the contingency table again
contingency_table <- table(cleaned_data$Attendance, cleaned_data$Meaning.Level)

# Check the contingency table
print(contingency_table)

# Run the Chi-Square test
chi_sq_test <- chisq.test(contingency_table)
print(chi_sq_test)


```

```{r}
# Stacked Bar Plot for Attendance and Meaning Level
library(ggplot2)

# Remove rows with NA values in Attendance or Meaning Level
cleaned_data <- na.omit(scale_data_1[, c("Attendance", "Meaning.Level")])

# Ensure Meaning Level is treated as a factor
cleaned_data$Meaning.Level <- as.factor(cleaned_data$Meaning.Level)

# Stacked Bar Plot to visualize the relationship between Attendance and Meaning Level
ggplot(cleaned_data, aes(x = Attendance, fill = Meaning.Level)) +
  geom_bar(position = "stack") +  # Stack the bars
  labs(title = "Stacked Bar Plot of Attendance and Meaning Level", 
       x = "Attendance", 
       y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3")  # Use a color palette for better color differentiation


```
